methodology: ChatGPT-reviewed macro snapshot. The browser does not scrape or score the source page. Macro readings are interpreted into regime blocks and Power Stack theme transmission, then stored in GitHub. Base Conviction is never overwritten; the macro overlay is capped at +/-1.00.

drivers.title: ISM Manufacturing
drivers.detail: July Manufacturing PMI 55.6, New Orders 56.7 and Production 58.5 point to a real manufacturing expansion rather than a headline-only improvement.

drivers.title: Services demand
drivers.detail: July Services PMI 54.1 with Business Activity 59.1 and New Orders 57.2 keeps services demand in expansion.

drivers.title: Growth nowcast moderated
drivers.detail: Atlanta Fed GDPNow for Q3 eased to 4.0% from 4.3%; industrial production rose 0.2% in July, slightly below the 0.3% forecast.

drivers.title: CPI cooled
drivers.detail: July CPI was 3.4% YoY and core CPI 2.5%, both slightly cooler than June.

drivers.title: PPI softened
drivers.detail: July PPI was 0.0% MoM and 4.7% YoY, down from 5.5% YoY previously.

drivers.title: ISM price pressure remains high
drivers.detail: Manufacturing Prices remained 71.1 and Services Prices rose to 70.3; Michigan 1-year inflation expectations were 4.3%.

drivers.title: Payroll shock
drivers.detail: July nonfarm payrolls were -23K versus 85K expected; wage growth slowed to 0.1% MoM and 3.2% YoY.

drivers.title: Services employment contracted
drivers.detail: ISM Services Employment fell to 47.4, while Manufacturing Employment improved to 52.8.

drivers.title: Claims remain contained
drivers.detail: Initial claims were 209K with continuing claims 1.777M, preventing the labour signal from becoming outright recessionary.

drivers.title: 10-year yield elevated
drivers.detail: The US 10Y was 4.72%; TLT was down 3.38% MoM and 5.21% YoY.

drivers.title: Long auction yields rose
drivers.detail: The latest 10-year auction cleared at 4.683% and the 30-year auction at 5.216%, reinforcing restrictive long-duration financing conditions.

drivers.title: Broad credit remains tight
drivers.detail: IG OAS was 0.81 and HY OAS 2.70; HY sat near the 9th percentile of its three-year range.

drivers.title: Weakest borrowers are stressed
drivers.detail: CCC & Lower OAS reached 10.18, around the 97th percentile of its three-year range, creating a sharp quality split inside credit.

drivers.title: Retail sales missed
drivers.detail: July Retail Sales fell 0.6% MoM versus +0.1% expected; Core Retail Sales fell 0.3% and Retail Control fell 0.4%.

drivers.title: Sentiment weakened
drivers.detail: Michigan Consumer Sentiment fell to 51.0 and expectations to 50.6.

drivers.title: Starts contracted
drivers.detail: July Housing Starts fell 12.4% MoM to 1.239M versus 1.340M expected.

drivers.title: Permits improved
drivers.detail: Building Permits rose 5.0% MoM to 1.443M, while Pending Home Sales fell 2.3% and NAHB remained weak at 35.

drivers.title: Inventory picture reversed
drivers.detail: The prior EIA report showed a 17.423M crude build, while the latest API estimate showed a 3.280M draw. The next EIA release is the cleaner confirmation point.

drivers.title: Positioning cooled
drivers.detail: CFTC crude net longs fell to 99.2K from 112.4K in the prior week.

drivers.title: Nasdaq positioning turned more negative
drivers.detail: CFTC Nasdaq 100 speculative positioning moved to -39.3K from -14.6K.

drivers.title: S&P positioning improved
drivers.detail: CFTC S&P 500 speculative positioning improved to +11.3K from -27.3K, while copper and gold net longs increased.

themes.regime: mixed: strong demand, restrictive discount rate

signals.title: Manufacturing expansion supports AI capex
signals.detail: ISM Manufacturing 55.6, New Orders 56.7 and Production 58.5 support physical AI and data-centre investment.

signals.title: Long rates pressure long-duration multiples
signals.detail: US 10Y near 4.72% and weak TLT performance keep the discount-rate headwind elevated.

signals.title: Labour and consumer slowdown add demand risk
signals.detail: Weak payrolls, ISM Services Employment below 50 and soft retail sales increase late-cycle risk.

signals.title: Credit quality split matters
signals.detail: Broad HY remains calm but CCC stress argues for profitable, well-funded infrastructure leaders over speculative balance sheets.

watch.title: Capex can stay strong while multiples compress
watch.detail: Separate physical AI/data-centre order growth from equity duration risk.
watch.nextTest: Next hyperscaler capex/guidance cycle and long-end Treasury move.

signals.title: Industrial expansion supports grid bottlenecks
signals.detail: Manufacturing production, orders and backlog are expanding, supporting electrical equipment and transmission demand.

signals.title: High equipment prices favour pricing power
signals.detail: ISM price and supply signals remain elevated, helping scarce equipment vendors more than low-margin contractors.

signals.title: Long rates remain a headwind
signals.detail: Restrictive long yields pressure valuation and financing for rate-sensitive projects.

signals.title: Tail credit stress is contained
signals.detail: Broad IG/HY spreads remain benign, limiting financing stress for high-quality infrastructure incumbents.

watch.title: Order strength vs valuation
watch.detail: Strong backlog does not immunise premium electrical names from higher real/nominal discount rates.
watch.nextTest: Next utility/electrical earnings and 10Y/30Y yield trend.

signals.title: Power demand remains structurally supportive
signals.detail: Expansion in industrial activity supports the need for reliable generation capacity.

signals.title: Rates punish development-stage nuclear
signals.detail: High long-end yields are much more negative for pre-revenue SMR developers than for profitable operators/components.

signals.title: Weakest-borrower stress raises financing bar
signals.detail: CCC spread stress increases the value of backlog, cash flow and government-supported funding.

watch.title: Do not treat nuclear as one macro trade
watch.detail: BWXT/CEG/CGN Power and OKLO/SMR should respond differently to the same rates and credit regime.
watch.nextTest: Company-specific financing, contracts and project milestones.

signals.title: Power-system demand supports fuel-chain scarcity
signals.detail: Industrial expansion and grid-load growth reinforce the longer-duration nuclear fuel thesis.

signals.title: Commodity/fuel exposure is less duration-sensitive
signals.detail: High rates are a smaller headwind for uranium producers/fuel suppliers than for development-stage reactor equities.

watch.title: Macro is secondary to fuel-cycle fundamentals
watch.detail: Contracting, enrichment scarcity, utility inventories and project execution should dominate the macro overlay.
watch.nextTest: Uranium contracting, HALEU/enrichment developments and producer guidance.

signals.title: Manufacturing expansion helps cyclical demand
signals.detail: Strong ISM manufacturing is supportive for industrial energy demand.

signals.title: Weak retail and labour temper demand
signals.detail: Consumer and labour softness argue against reading strong manufacturing as broad demand acceleration.

signals.title: Inventory signal is conflicted
signals.detail: A huge EIA build was followed by an API draw; the near-term crude balance needs confirmation.

watch.title: Crude and products can diverge
watch.detail: Inventory, refinery utilisation and product tightness should be read separately for producers, pipelines and refiners.
watch.nextTest: Next EIA crude, gasoline, distillate and refinery-utilisation release.

signals.title: Manufacturing expansion supports industrial metals
signals.detail: Orders, production and backlog are constructive for copper and electrification-linked demand.

signals.title: Housing and consumer softness offset part of the impulse
signals.detail: Weak starts, pending sales and retail reduce broad cyclical confirmation.

signals.title: High yields remain a valuation and dollar headwind
signals.detail: Restrictive long rates can pressure duration-sensitive miners and non-yielding metals.

signals.title: Copper positioning strengthened
signals.detail: CFTC copper net longs rose to 80.4K from 77.1K.

watch.title: Copper is cleaner than broad metals
watch.detail: Power/grid capex has a stronger structural read-through to copper than to palladium or precious metals.
watch.nextTest: China/global industrial data and copper inventory/price confirmation.

signals.title: Factory expansion helps automation demand
signals.detail: Manufacturing New Orders and Production are above 50 and accelerating.

signals.title: Long-duration robotics valuations remain rate-sensitive
signals.detail: High long-end yields reduce tolerance for distant cash flows.

signals.title: Quality matters
signals.detail: Tail credit stress favours profitable automation incumbents over capital-hungry speculative robotics names.

watch.title: Adoption order still matters
watch.detail: Warehouse/fixed automation can monetise before general-purpose humanoids even in a supportive manufacturing regime.
watch.nextTest: Orders, backlog and commercial deployment evidence.

signals.title: Industrial and data-centre activity supports water/cooling demand
signals.detail: Manufacturing expansion and continued AI infrastructure buildout support cooling, reuse and water-treatment equipment.

signals.title: Higher yields restrain project multiples
signals.detail: Long-end rates remain a valuation and financing headwind.

signals.title: Broad financing conditions remain workable
signals.detail: Tight IG/HY spreads offset some rate pressure for established infrastructure operators.

watch.title: Separate recurring water economics from AI cooling beta
watch.detail: ECL/XYL and MOD/VRT should not receive the same macro interpretation.
watch.nextTest: Data-centre capex and industrial water/reuse order growth.

signals.title: Weak consumer data is a mild demand headwind
signals.detail: Retail and sentiment weakness are negative for discretionary food chains but less important for essential agricultural inputs.

signals.title: High financing costs pressure farm/project economics
signals.detail: Restrictive long rates are a modest negative for equipment and capital-intensive agriculture.

signals.title: Sticky input prices preserve pricing complexity
signals.detail: High upstream prices can support nominal revenue but also squeeze margins.

watch.title: Weather and crop fundamentals dominate macro
watch.detail: WASDE, crop yields, fertiliser and commodity balances should override small macro changes.
watch.nextTest: WASDE/crop conditions and company-specific volume/margin guidance.

signals.title: Weak consumer/labour data increases defensive value
signals.detail: Healthcare demand is less cyclical than discretionary spending, improving relative resilience.

signals.title: Long rates still matter for valuation
signals.detail: High discount rates remain a mild headwind for premium-growth healthcare equities.

watch.title: Company execution dominates macro
watch.detail: Drug efficacy, supply, reimbursement and adoption should matter more than the macro overlay.
watch.nextTest: Prescription/adoption data, supply capacity and payer coverage.
